# Tool reference

<!-- Generated by `make docs` (go run ./cmd/gen-tool-docs) from the tool definitions. Do not edit by hand. -->

hive-mcp has **24 tools** in **5 toolsets**: 13 read and 11 write. It also has **5 prompts**.

Each tool is labelled with the setting it needs:

| Label | Registered when |
|---|---|
| 🟢 read | Always |
| 🟠 write | `HIVE_ALLOW_WRITES=true` |

Every tool also needs its toolset to be enabled in `HIVE_TOOLSETS`, which enables all toolsets by default. Temperatures are in °C, and heating targets go from 5 to 32 in steps of 0.5. Times are in the home's local time. Read tools return compact summaries, and many take `raw: true` for Hive's full objects and `fresh: true` to skip the short cache.

## Contents

- [`home`](#home): Login, a one-call overview of the home, the list of Hive devices with batteries and signal, and holiday mode.
- [`heating`](#heating): Heating zones and radiator valve (TRV) zones: temperatures, modes and schedules; set the temperature or mode, boost and cancel a boost.
- [`hotwater`](#hotwater): Hot water: status and schedule; switch it on, off or back to its schedule, boost and cancel a boost.
- [`devices`](#devices): Smart plugs, lights and sensors: on or off, power use, brightness, colour temperature, open or closed.
- [`raw`](#raw): A raw API escape hatch for anything the other tools don't cover. It is limited to GET requests unless writes are enabled.
- [Prompts](#prompts)

## home

Login, a one-call overview of the home, the list of Hive devices with batteries and signal, and holiday mode.

| Tool | Access | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [`hive_auth_complete`](#hive_auth_complete) | 🟢 read | Finish Hive login |
| [`hive_auth_start`](#hive_auth_start) | 🟢 read | Start Hive login |
| [`hive_auth_status`](#hive_auth_status) | 🟢 read | Hive login status |
| [`hive_cancel_holiday_mode`](#hive_cancel_holiday_mode) | 🟠 write | Cancel holiday mode |
| [`hive_get_holiday_mode`](#hive_get_holiday_mode) | 🟢 read | Get holiday mode |
| [`hive_get_overview`](#hive_get_overview) | 🟢 read | Home overview |
| [`hive_list_devices`](#hive_list_devices) | 🟢 read | List Hive devices |
| [`hive_set_holiday_mode`](#hive_set_holiday_mode) | 🟠 write | Set holiday mode |

### hive_auth_complete

🟢 read

Finish a login started with hive_auth_start by giving the code Hive texted to the account's phone. This also registers the server as a remembered device, so it won't need a code again.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | yes | The code from the text message Hive sent to the account's phone |

### hive_auth_start

🟢 read

Start logging this server in to Hive with HIVE_USERNAME and HIVE_PASSWORD. If this server is already a remembered device, that's the whole login. Otherwise Hive texts a code to the account's phone: ask the user for it and pass it to hive_auth_complete within about three minutes. Only use this when the user asks to log in or a tool says the server isn't logged in; it sends a real text message.

_No arguments._

### hive_auth_status

🟢 read

Show whether this server is logged in to Hive: the account, whether this server is a remembered device (so it can log in again without an SMS code), when the current token expires and any login error. Never shows passwords, tokens or device secrets.

_No arguments._

### hive_cancel_holiday_mode

🟠 write

Cancel holiday mode, so the heating and hot water go back to their normal settings straight away.

_No arguments._

### hive_get_holiday_mode

🟢 read

Show whether holiday mode is set: when it starts and ends and the temperature the heating holds while you're away.

_No arguments._

### hive_get_overview

🟢 read

A one-call snapshot of the home: every heating zone and TRV zone (current and target temperature, mode, boost, whether it's calling for heat), the hot water, plugs, lights and sensors, holiday mode, and anything that needs attention: low batteries, offline devices and discontinued hardware. A good first call.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fresh` | boolean |  | Ask Hive again instead of using a reading from the last few seconds (HIVE_CACHE_SECONDS) |

### hive_list_devices

🟢 read

List the Hive hardware: hub, thermostats, boiler module, radiator valves (TRVs), plugs, bulbs and sensors, with online status, battery level, signal strength, model and firmware. Filter by type, low battery or offline.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fresh` | boolean |  | Ask Hive again instead of using a reading from the last few seconds (HIVE_CACHE_SECONDS) |
| `low_battery` | boolean |  | Only battery devices at or below 25% |
| `offline` | boolean |  | Only devices Hive says are offline |
| `raw` | boolean |  | Return Hive's full objects instead of compact summaries (much larger) |
| `type` | string |  | Only devices of this type, for example trv, thermostatui, boilermodule, hub, activeplug, warmwhitelight, contactsensor |

### hive_set_holiday_mode

🟠 write

Set holiday mode: from start (default now) until end, the heating holds one temperature, then the normal settings resume. Replaces any holiday mode already set. Confirm the dates and temperature with the user first.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `end` | string | yes | When it ends and the normal schedule resumes, as YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM in the home's local time |
| `temperature` | number (5–32) | yes | Temperature to keep the home at while away, in °C (5 to 32 in steps of 0.5; frost protection is usually 7) |
| `start` | string |  | When holiday mode starts, as YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM in the home's local time (default now) |

## heating

Heating zones and radiator valve (TRV) zones: temperatures, modes and schedules; set the temperature or mode, boost and cancel a boost.

| Tool | Access | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [`hive_boost_heating`](#hive_boost_heating) | 🟠 write | Boost heating |
| [`hive_cancel_heating_boost`](#hive_cancel_heating_boost) | 🟠 write | Cancel heating boost |
| [`hive_get_heating`](#hive_get_heating) | 🟢 read | Get heating |
| [`hive_get_heating_schedule`](#hive_get_heating_schedule) | 🟢 read | Get heating schedule |
| [`hive_list_trvs`](#hive_list_trvs) | 🟢 read | List radiator valves |
| [`hive_set_heating_mode`](#hive_set_heating_mode) | 🟠 write | Set heating mode |
| [`hive_set_heating_temperature`](#hive_set_heating_temperature) | 🟠 write | Set heating temperature |

### hive_boost_heating

🟠 write

Boost a zone: heat to a temperature for a number of minutes, then go back to the previous mode. Replaces any boost already running.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `temperature` | number (5–32) | yes | Temperature to boost to, in °C (5 to 32 in steps of 0.5) |
| `minutes` | integer (1–360) |  | How long to boost for, in minutes (default 60, at most 360) |
| `zone` | string |  | Heating zone or TRV zone, by name (for example "Heating" or "Bedroom") or ID. Can be left out when there's only one. See hive_get_heating |

### hive_cancel_heating_boost

🟠 write

Stop a zone's boost early and go back to the mode (and, for manual or off, the temperature) it had before.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zone` | string |  | Heating zone or TRV zone, by name (for example "Heating" or "Bedroom") or ID. Can be left out when there's only one. See hive_get_heating |

### hive_get_heating

🟢 read

Show the heating: for each heating zone (a Hive thermostat) and TRV zone (Hive radiator valves), the current temperature, target temperature, mode (schedule, manual, off or boost), boost time left, whether it's calling for heat, what the schedule asks for now and next, and thermostat or valve batteries.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fresh` | boolean |  | Ask Hive again instead of using a reading from the last few seconds (HIVE_CACHE_SECONDS) |
| `raw` | boolean |  | Return Hive's full objects instead of compact summaries (much larger) |
| `zone` | string |  | Only this zone, by name or ID (default every heating zone and TRV zone) |

### hive_get_heating_schedule

🟢 read

Show a zone's weekly heating schedule: for each day, the periods and the target temperature for each, in the home's local time. Also says what the schedule asks for now and when it next changes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zone` | string |  | Heating zone or TRV zone, by name (for example "Heating" or "Bedroom") or ID. Can be left out when there's only one. See hive_get_heating |

### hive_list_trvs

🟢 read

List the Hive radiator valves (TRVs) by zone: each zone's temperature, target and mode, and each valve's battery, signal, online status, calibration, mounting and child lock.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fresh` | boolean |  | Ask Hive again instead of using a reading from the last few seconds (HIVE_CACHE_SECONDS) |

### hive_set_heating_mode

🟠 write

Switch a zone between schedule (follow the weekly schedule), manual (hold one temperature) and off (frost protection only). Cancels a boost.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `"schedule"` \| `"manual"` \| `"off"` | yes | schedule (follow the heating schedule), manual (hold one temperature) or off (frost protection only) |
| `temperature` | number (5–32) |  | With manual: the temperature to hold, in °C (5 to 32 in steps of 0.5). Default: the zone's current target |
| `zone` | string |  | Heating zone or TRV zone, by name (for example "Heating" or "Bedroom") or ID. Can be left out when there's only one. See hive_get_heating |

### hive_set_heating_temperature

🟠 write

Set a zone's target temperature. In schedule mode this lasts until the next scheduled change, like turning the thermostat dial; pass mode=manual to hold it. If the zone is off, the target is saved but nothing heats until the mode changes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `temperature` | number (5–32) | yes | Target temperature in °C, 5 to 32 in steps of 0.5 |
| `mode` | `"manual"` \| `"schedule"` |  | Also switch mode: manual (hold this temperature) or schedule (just until the next scheduled change, as turning the dial does) |
| `zone` | string |  | Heating zone or TRV zone, by name (for example "Heating" or "Bedroom") or ID. Can be left out when there's only one. See hive_get_heating |

## hotwater

Hot water: status and schedule; switch it on, off or back to its schedule, boost and cancel a boost.

| Tool | Access | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [`hive_boost_hot_water`](#hive_boost_hot_water) | 🟠 write | Boost hot water |
| [`hive_cancel_hot_water_boost`](#hive_cancel_hot_water_boost) | 🟠 write | Cancel hot water boost |
| [`hive_get_hot_water`](#hive_get_hot_water) | 🟢 read | Get hot water |
| [`hive_get_hot_water_schedule`](#hive_get_hot_water_schedule) | 🟢 read | Get hot water schedule |
| [`hive_set_hot_water_mode`](#hive_set_hot_water_mode) | 🟠 write | Set hot water mode |

### hive_boost_hot_water

🟠 write

Heat the hot water now for a number of minutes, then go back to the previous mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minutes` | integer (1–360) |  | How long to heat the water for, in minutes (default 60, at most 360) |

### hive_cancel_hot_water_boost

🟠 write

Stop a hot water boost early and go back to the previous mode.

_No arguments._

### hive_get_hot_water

🟢 read

Show the hot water: whether it's heating now, the mode (schedule, on, off or boost), boost time left, and what the schedule asks for now and next.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fresh` | boolean |  | Ask Hive again instead of using a reading from the last few seconds (HIVE_CACHE_SECONDS) |
| `raw` | boolean |  | Return Hive's full objects instead of compact summaries (much larger) |

### hive_get_hot_water_schedule

🟢 read

Show the weekly hot water schedule: for each day, when the hot water is on and off, in the home's local time.

_No arguments._

### hive_set_hot_water_mode

🟠 write

Switch the hot water on (it stays on until changed), off, or back to its schedule. Cancels a boost. For a limited time, use hive_boost_hot_water instead of on.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `"on"` \| `"off"` \| `"schedule"` | yes | on (stay on until changed), off, or schedule (follow the hot water schedule) |

## devices

Smart plugs, lights and sensors: on or off, power use, brightness, colour temperature, open or closed.

| Tool | Access | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [`hive_list_smart_devices`](#hive_list_smart_devices) | 🟢 read | List plugs, lights and sensors |
| [`hive_set_light`](#hive_set_light) | 🟠 write | Control a light |
| [`hive_set_plug`](#hive_set_plug) | 🟠 write | Switch a smart plug |

### hive_list_smart_devices

🟢 read

List Hive smart plugs (on or off, power use), lights (on or off, brightness, colour temperature) and sensors (window and door sensors open or closed, motion sensors), with online status and batteries.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fresh` | boolean |  | Ask Hive again instead of using a reading from the last few seconds (HIVE_CACHE_SECONDS) |
| `kind` | `"plugs"` \| `"lights"` \| `"sensors"` |  | Only plugs, lights or sensors (default all) |
| `raw` | boolean |  | Return Hive's full objects instead of compact summaries (much larger) |

### hive_set_light

🟠 write

Switch a Hive light on or off, and set its brightness or (for tuneable and colour bulbs) its white colour temperature.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `brightness` | integer (5–100) |  | Brightness in percent, 5 to 100 (rounded to the nearest 5, as the Hive app does) |
| `colour_temperature` | integer (2700–6535) |  | White colour temperature in kelvin, for tuneable and colour bulbs: about 2700 (warm) to 6500 (cool) |
| `light` | string |  | Light, by name or ID (see hive_list_smart_devices). Can be left out when there's only one |
| `on` | boolean |  | true to switch on, false to switch off. Setting a brightness or colour temperature also switches the light on |

### hive_set_plug

🟠 write

Switch a Hive smart plug on or off. Check what's plugged in with the user before switching it off.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | true to switch the plug on, false to switch it off |
| `plug` | string |  | Smart plug, by name or ID (see hive_list_smart_devices). Can be left out when there's only one |

## raw

A raw API escape hatch for anything the other tools don't cover. It is limited to GET requests unless writes are enabled.

| Tool | Access | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [`hive_api_request`](#hive_api_request) | 🟢 read | Raw Hive API request |

### hive_api_request

🟢 read · destructive

Call any path of Hive's API (the undocumented "beekeeper" API the Hive app uses) directly, for anything the other tools don't cover, such as /nodes/all, /devices, /products or /actions. All methods are allowed. Changes go straight to Hive with no checks, so confirm them with the user first.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Path relative to https://beekeeper.hivehome.com/1.0, for example /nodes/all or /holiday-mode |
| `body` | any |  | JSON request body for POST, PUT and DELETE |
| `method` | `"GET"` \| `"POST"` \| `"PUT"` \| `"DELETE"` |  | HTTP method: GET (default), POST, PUT or DELETE |
| `query` | object |  | Query string parameters |

## Prompts

Prompts are ready-made requests that tell the model which tools to call and what to report. In Claude Code they appear as slash commands, such as `/mcp__hive__home_check`.

### going_away

Set the home up for a trip: holiday mode with a frost-safe temperature, and a check of anything left on.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `leave` |  | When you leave (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM; default now) |
| `return` | yes | When you're back (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM) |

### home_check

A quick check of the home: temperatures, what the heating and hot water are doing, holiday mode, and any low batteries or offline devices.

### hot_water_now

Get hot water for a bath or shower: check whether it's already on and boost it if not.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `minutes` |  | How long to heat the water for, in minutes (default 30) |

### schedule_review

Review the heating and hot water schedules for comfort and wasted energy, and suggest changes.

### warm_up

Boost the heating to a comfortable temperature for a while, checking the current state first.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `temperature` |  | Temperature to boost to in °C (default 21) |
| `minutes` |  | How long for, in minutes (default 60) |
| `zone` |  | Which heating zone (default the main one) |
